articles.author: tessa-wren
articles.title: Game of the Week: Sunyshore brings a complete offense to Mossdeep’s bye test
articles.dek: The 11–3 Starseekers have a productive runner, four touchdown catches from 88 Special, and one remaining route to the first seed. Mossdeep can settle the race with a win or tie.

body.text: Sunyshore arrives at Mossdeep with a convincing answer to the simplest question about this matchup: can the Starseekers do enough on offense to make the Eclipse defend a complete game? They just ran for 175 yards, passed for 279 and scored forty-one against Rustboro. Myles Gabite supplied 144 rushing yards. DeZhaun Watzon threw four touchdown passes, all to 88 Special, while three other receivers also made substantial contributions. Karson Jones has several productive ways to begin the conversation.

The next question is harder. Can Sunyshore keep Dram Marino and Accel BeckhmJr from turning a good Starseekers possession into a brief interruption? Mossdeep has scored 185 points in its last three games. Marino threw seven touchdown passes against Petalburg, then seven more at Canalave. BeckhmJr followed five touchdown catches with four, including a sixty-one-yard score. An opponent can play respectable offense and still spend most of this game needing the ball back.

I pick Mossdeep 38, Sunyshore 21. The Starseekers have the balance to make the unbeaten team work, and their eleven victories deserve more consideration than a glance at the Eclipse's latest margin. I favor Mossdeep because its passing production has remained both spectacular and careful. Marino has fifty-four touchdown passes against three interceptions. Sunyshore still has Serp Gardener unavailable for one reported week, removing a coverage option just as the league's most productive passing combination comes into view.
The bye is available at Mossdeep's own stadium

Mossdeep is 14–0 and has already won Hoenn East. Sunyshore is 11–3 and has already won Sinnoh East. A Mossdeep win or tie secures the Hoenn–Sinnoh first seed and the opening-round bye. Sunyshore has to win to keep its route open, then continue winning at Pastoria and Veilstone while hoping Mossdeep loses its final two games against Sootopolis and Lavaridge. In that possible 14–3 tie, this head-to-head result would belong to the Starseekers.

That gives both coaches a specific reward to discuss. Michael Dorrill can give his players a week without an opening-round game by winning now. Jones can keep a difficult pursuit alive while proving his team can beat the conference leader on the road. Neither needs to invent a season-defining label for an ordinary fixture. The standings have already provided the stakes.

“We've earned the right to walk in there expecting to play well,” Jones said. “That expectation has to show up in the blocking, in the routes, in the way we finish the tackle. You want attention? Give people a reason to keep watching the next snap.” His team supplied those reasons against Rustboro after falling behind seven-zero. The forty-one unanswered points came from sustained productivity rather than a series of gifts: neither club lost a turnover.
Gabite gives Sunyshore a way to choose the next down

Gabite carried sixteen times for 144 yards and two touchdowns. His twenty-six-yard run up the middle tied the Rustboro game in the first quarter, and his three-yard fourth-down run supplied Sunyshore's final touchdown late in the fourth. The Starseekers could use him for an explosive answer and for the short finish of a longer possession. That combination made Watzon's passing work considerably easier to defend in theory than in practice.

The performance was also a substantial expansion of Gabite's season production. He now has 269 rushing yards on forty-two carries, meaning more than half those yards arrived against the Stone. I would treat that as a powerful recent observation and still ask him to repeat the useful parts. One afternoon does not establish that nine yards a carry is now Sunyshore's ordinary expectation.

Mossdeep gave Canalave ninety-three rushing yards on thirty-four attempts. Seismitoad accounted for eighty-one of them on twenty-two carries. That is a more restrained defensive result than the Bulwark's 334 total yards might suggest. Sunyshore will need its runs to create favorable passing situations, rather than simply demonstrating patience while the scoreboard moves against it.

My rushing target for the Starseekers is 120 yards. That would be below their Rustboro total but enough to give the passing game genuine assistance. It matters how those yards arrive: a useful first-down gain gives Watzon choices, while a late run against a large deficit may improve the total without helping the next scoring chance. I will also watch whether Sunyshore can avoid asking for repeated difficult third-down completions.
Four touchdown catches do not account for the whole passing game

88 Special caught six passes for seventy-seven yards and four touchdowns against Rustboro. The scores traveled ten, seventeen, twenty-five and eight yards, with two to each broad side of the field. Watzon did not need the same distance or the same side every time he looked for the receiver. Mossdeep has to defend the finishing route without allowing the other targets to move the possession into range.

Jolt Vick had six catches for eighty-seven yards. Fera LaGatr caught six for seventy-six. MF STOMP added four catches for thirty-four, and BAXXED? caught the remaining completion. Those twenty-three completed passes gave Sunyshore several productive destinations. Calling for more attention on 88 Special is an understandable opening instruction; the following instruction must explain who handles the other receivers.

Watzon finished twenty-three of thirty without an interception. That accuracy is particularly useful against a Mossdeep defense that recorded seven sacks against Petalburg and four at Canalave. Joey Sporeter had two sacks in the latter game and recovered Canalave's lost fumble. Sunyshore cannot assume that a covered first option will leave unlimited time to locate the second.

The Eclipse's practical target is to hold Sunyshore below forty percent on third down. Rustboro allowed three conversions in seven chances, but the Starseekers did enough work before third down that the offense never depended on a large volume of conversions. Mossdeep needs to make those late downs both more frequent and less manageable. That is a defensive task involving the run fits, coverage and rush together.
BeckhmJr makes an ordinary coverage error unusually expensive

BeckhmJr caught ten passes for 270 yards at Canalave. His four touchdowns included the sixty-one-yard throw deep left early in the second quarter, a twenty-nine-yard score deep right, a six-yard finish short left and a twenty-one-yard touchdown deep right. The variety matters. Sunyshore has to limit both the immediate explosive gain and the shorter completion that finishes a possession already moving successfully.

His season line is seventy-five catches, 1,875 yards and thirty-one receiving touchdowns. Marino has 4,025 passing yards. Those totals make a plan built entirely around waiting for a bad throw difficult to defend. Mossdeep's quarterback has thrown only three interceptions in 348 attempts, and Sunyshore did not force a giveaway against Rustboro. The visitors need successful coverage and pressure on ordinary plays as well as whatever exceptional opportunity appears.

Sunyshore should also account for Ninjulio Jones, who caught four passes for seventy-two yards and a touchdown at Canalave. Gronkaludon caught all three of his targets, including a touchdown. Shawn Mareman added a receiving score. An extra defender attending to BeckhmJr has to come from somewhere, and Marino has just demonstrated several ways to use the remaining space.

I want Mossdeep to allow no more than two sacks. That is a concrete protection standard against a defense that held Rustboro to five first downs and one third-down conversion in eleven attempts. The Eclipse allowed one sack in Canalave's box score and scored without punting. Sunyshore offers a more demanding test of how consistently that protection can preserve Marino's choices.
The injury reports improve in places without settling the lineup

Gardener's remaining absence is Sunyshore's clearest continuing concern. FLOAT SZN no longer has a reported week of absence, while Scol Alexander's new minor designation carries no remaining absence. Those updates improve the available information without establishing a starting assignment or the workload any player will receive.

Mossdeep's Marshall Flock and Luvrelle Revis likewise have no remaining reported absence. Ninjaskamara is still listed for one week and Richard Furman for two. Mareman and Poury Holt have handled useful backfield work during the absences, but the Eclipse's latest wins have been driven overwhelmingly by the passing game. Sunyshore's task is to force more possessions in which that passing advantage has to be earned over several snaps.

“We gave up a touchdown,” Dorrill said of the 51–7 win at Canalave. “That possession is in the review. So is the missed extra point. The next opponent doesn't owe us the same mistakes, and the score doesn't excuse ours.” Sunyshore's six-touchdown performance gives that insistence a practical setting. An eleven-win visitor can make small failures cost more than they did against an offense that reached the end zone once.

For Sunyshore to win, Gabite must help the offense remain balanced, Watzon must keep finding the productive receiver without giveaways, and the defense must hold Mossdeep to substantially fewer touchdown passes than its recent seven-per-game rate. My checkable ceiling for the visitors is four passing touchdowns allowed. They can then try to win a game in which their own offense reaches the thirties.

I expect Mossdeep's receivers to exceed the visitors' ability to trade scoring possessions for a full afternoon. Sunyshore can move the ball and score enough to demand attention, but Marino's season-long combination of production and ball security gives the Eclipse the stronger way to finish. Mossdeep 38, Sunyshore 21, with the first seed and bye secured at home.
